title: Consensus Health Index: tier-aware region arbiter combining p50/p95 latency and path loss
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Introduce a Consensus Health Index (CHI) used by the region arbiter to pick POPs and tier routes. CHI fuses latency quantiles (p50, p95) with network path signals (packet loss, reorders/jitter, and TCP RTO signals) into a single, tier-aware score. Goal: reduce visible latency tail regressions and avoid repeated suboptimal routing during transient network blips while preserving cost/tier preferences. This ticket covers spec, scoring function, smoothing & hysteresis, API surface for runtime flags, rollout plan, and monitoring/alerting changes.
updates: 2025-11-18: RFC draft posted to Confluence: /confluence/redwood/CHI-rfc. Initial scoring proposal fuses EWMA of p50/p95 with loss-rate penalty and a tier-penalty multiplier. Asked infra telemetry for historical windows (1m, 5m, 15m).

2025-11-21: Telemetry team provided sample datasets (regionA/regionB) and a Kibana dashboard proof-of-concept: https://grafana.internal.redwood/board/chi-smoke. Early tests show p95 spikes correlate with tiny increases in retransmits; p50 remains stable in several incidents.

2025-11-25: Design review with PM/Product (Lina Chen) and SRE (Noah Feldman). Decision: use dual-quantile term (alpha * p50 + beta * p95) with beta > alpha, plus multiplicative loss factor (1 + gamma * loss_pct). Tier multiplier reduces sensitivity for lower-cost tiers so cheaper pools are not evicted on small spikes. Documented trade-offs: reduces oscillation but can delay fail-over for catastrophic region failures. Added hysteresis: require CHI > threshold for T consecutive windows or exceed by margin M to trigger failover immediately.

2025-11-30: Implementation spike started. Created prototype in service-region-orchestrator (branch: feat/chi-arbiter). Implemented CHI calculator module with configurable weights and decay half-life. Unit tests added for weighting edge cases.

2025-12-02: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/region-orchestrator/pull/864. Initial code review feedback from Samuel Park: simplify smoothing code to reuse existing EWMA util and add explicit saturation clamps to avoid NaNs. Marco addressed comments and pushed updates.

2025-12-03: Canary plan approved by SRE and Product. Small-scale canary will run against 5% of routing decisions for 24h in us-east-1 and eu-west-1 with detailed logging and a revert flag. Observability tasks scheduled to add CHI time-series and alert rules for sustained CHI degradation and repeated toggling.
Follow-ups: investigate adding TCP RTT variance and BBR signals for further signal richness (deferred to ENG-139900).
implementation_notes: Scoring formula (initial): CHI = tier_scale * (alpha * EWMA(p50_ms) + beta * EWMA(p95_ms)) * (1 + gamma * loss_fraction) + jitter_penalty
Suggested default weights: alpha=0.3, beta=0.7, gamma=4.0, tier_scale=1.0 for premium, 1.25 for standard, 1.5 for economy. These are tunable via runtime config.
Smoothing: use EWMA windows of 10s for rapid detection and 5m for stability; the decision layer should compute short and long windows and require consistency or exceedance margin before switching.
Hysteresis: once a region is deprioritized due to CHI, enforce minimum cool-down of 60s and require CHI improvement beyond 20% over previous baseline before re-including.

Fallbacks: when CHI indicates region health is poor, prefer fallback to same-tier variant in another region. If no same-tier capacity, fall back to compatible model variant (e.g., int8 quantized variant) with lower resource needs following policy in runtime-compat.

Instrumentation: export raw inputs (p50, p95, loss_pct, jitter) and final CHI per decision to tracing spans and metrics (histogram + gauge). Tag metrics with model, route, tenant, and chosen_pop for debugging.
Config surface: feature flag chi_enabled; tunables exposed in console: alpha,beta,gamma,tier_scales,short_window,long_window,chi_thresholds,hysteresis_seconds.
Runtime safety: enforce saturation and NaN guards; cap CHI to 1e6 to avoid numeric issues. Review required for potential style/format impacts on existing region selector API.
Database: store recent CHI state in redis path-state with TTL 5m; do not persist long-term to avoid stale state after cluster changes.
test_plan: Unit tests: CHI math with synthetic p50/p95/loss inputs covering edgecases (zero loss, 100% loss, extreme latencies).
Integration test: local region-orchestrator simulation with 3 pops, feed historical telemetry trace and assert routing decisions follow expected sequence under injected faults.
Load test: run canary for 5% of production decisions for 24h; run synthetic noise injection to ensure no oscillation at 1% noise level.
Chaos test: simulate complete region outage and confirm failover occurs within SLO when multiple windows exceed CHI thresholds.
Regression: verify fallbacks to model variants still respect tenant isolation and do not degrade SLO below configured tolerances.
Observability: verify CHI charts, decision traces, and alerts are created in Grafana/Tempo.
acceptance_criteria: CHI implementation merged behind feature flag and unit/integration tests green.

Canary ran for 24h with no customer-facing latency regressions and SRE sign-off. Metrics to validate: routing-flip-rate < 0.1 per minute, failed-requests delta < 0.5% vs baseline, steady-state p95 improved or unchanged for routes using CHI.
Console exposes basic tunables and CHI time-series for tenants to inspect.
Runbook updated with playbook steps: how to disable CHI, revert a canary, and emergency thresholds for manual override.
Post-mortem plan in place if we observe oscillations or regressions during canary.
